data.body:
Final rebar-debug report

Problem: two outer pytest tests launched executing nested pytest children without a private --basetemp, allowing those children to join pytest's user-global numbered temp root and delete cleanup-eligible trees belonging to another run.

Proven root cause: with the outer process isolated by its own --basetemp and PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT aimed at a controlled shared root containing pytest-0..pytest-3 plus an exact-byte sentinel in pytest-0, both affected outer tests returned rc=0 while their unowned inner child deleted the sentinel. Pytest 9.1.1 TempPathFactory.getbasetemp creates/registers numbered-root cleanup; pytest_sessionfinish skips cleanup only while _basetemp is None. This rules out the isolated outer session and the still-green target assertions, leaving the executing inner child as the deleting process.

Repair: tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py assigns the mixed-module child tmp_path/mixed-module-pytest via --basetemp; tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py assigns the bare-console-script child tmp_path/standalone-pytest. Both assert that the assigned child root materialized. Interpreter/console entrypoint, cwd, selector, plugins, environment filtering, return-code checks, and prior symptom assertions are unchanged. No production code, public API, config, or dependency changed.

Held-out oracle: before repair, the safe control passed and both affected parametrized cases failed because the sentinel disappeared. After repair all three cases passed and preserved sentinel existence, exact bytes, and shared-root entries. The oracle observes subprocess behavior and filesystem bytes, not source text.

Exact-defect mutations: reverting only the engine --basetemp repair produced .F. with only the engine case deleting the sentinel; restoring engine and reverting only the scripts-import repair produced ..F with only that case deleting the sentinel; restoring both returned 3 passed.

Caller/dependency safety: these are leaf test launchers, and no caller contract depends on deleting unrelated temp trees. Complete sibling inventory found three already-safe direct launchers with parent-owned basetemp; three collect-only launchers that never allocate TempPathFactory._basetemp; six pytester.runpytest_subprocess and four pytester.runpytest calls whose helper supplies basetemp; and only these two executing unsafe direct launchers. Literal pytest occurrences identified as test data were not launch sites. No residual affected launcher was observed.

Original-report replication and gates: controlled runtime reproduction observed deletion at both reported sites; focused inventory suite 92 passed, 2 skipped; held-out regression 3 passed; CI-default unit selection 10886 passed, 42 skipped, 8 deselected in 1782.45s; make lint PASS; make typecheck PASS; git diff --check PASS. Independent three-stage review: Stage 1 spec/architecture PASS, Stage 2 code/test quality PASS, Stage 3 domain integrity PASS; zero blocking and zero advisory findings.
